harnessHashes.app/src-tauri/src/main_window.rs: pre-build hash recorded in docs/evidence/kai-build-nobundle.log run

theAcceptanceQuestion: Aziz: the main window measured 345x9 in the running build — that number is the acceptance test.

measuredAnswer.what345x9ActuallyIs: the ISLAND's collapsed/hidden OS window (STRIP_W 240 x STRIP_H 6 logical, x the webview device scale factor 1.4354 = 345x9 physical). It is the companion pill, never the application window.
measuredAnswer.islandStays: 345 x 9 (collapsed companion strip) — correct and unchanged
measuredAnswer.note: width 1290 CSS is ABOVE the 1000 px threshold below which presence.css used to hide the navigation rail entirely.

chain: Windows display 110 % + accessibility text scale 130 % => the webview devicePixelRatio is 1.4354 while the window's own scale factor is 1.1046 (island.rs already documents this exact measurement).
tauri.conf.json declares the main window 1280x820 in LOGICAL units, and Tauri sized it with the window scale only => a 1414x906 physical client => a 985 CSS-px viewport.

app/src/shell/presence/presence.css had `@media(max-width:1000px){ ... .rail{display:none} ... }` => at 985 px the application's ONLY navigation was deleted, leaving the user with no way to reach any section, and a window that looked like a single squeezed panel.

fixes.what: apply_size(): sizes the window in WEBVIEW CSS pixels (win.scale_factor() * island::win_text_scale(), i.e. the real devicePixelRatio) so the viewport is the declared 1280x820, clamped to the monitor work area minus the MEASURED frame (outer-inner) and a 24 CSS-px margin, then centres it. Called from attach() and again on the FIRST show() (a never-shown window has no final DPI).
fixes.why: the declared size only means what it says if the webview's viewport is that size; this is the same correction island::apply_geometry already makes for the island.

fixes.what: the <=1000px rule no longer hides the rail: it becomes a compact icon rail (52px column, tighter padding).
fixes.why: hiding the only navigation is a defect at ANY width.

fixes.what: .rail: overflow-x:hidden added (overflow-y:auto in CSS forces overflow-x to auto, which produced twin scrollbars that ate the rail's width); scrollbar-width:none. Rail tiles .rb 46x46 -> 40x40 and gap 6 -> 4px.
fixes.why: 13 route buttons + orb + label at 46px need ~816 px of rail but only 670 px exist: the rail genuinely overflowed, so its last item was clipped. At 40px/4px the column needs ~662 px and fits.

liveVerification.method: docs/evidence/kai-window-acceptance.mjs (launches the real release binary detached, measures every kai.exe OS window rectangle via Win32 EnumWindows+GetWindowRect, reads each webview's own geometry over CDP, invokes the island's real open_main_window command and re-measures) and docs/evidence/kai-nav-proof.mjs (clicks every rail entry by its account name).

visionVerification.after: docs/evidence/nav-home-final.png (1290x705 CSS): 'YES there is a left navigation rail'; final pass: 'All rail icons are fully visible and fully inside the rail; nothing is cut off... No scrollbars appear on the rail — neither vertical nor horizontal.'

verdict: END-TO-END PROVEN for the window chain: island action -> Tauri command -> real window shown at a real size -> rail visible -> rail entries switch views against real Core. The one thing not exercised is a literal mouse click on the island button (the identical command was invoked in the island's own webview); a pointer-level run remains a nice-to-have, not a missing link. Bundling (`npx tauri build` WITH the NSIS installer) exits 1: makensis references core/bundle/agent/identity-model.d.ts while `beforeBuildCommand` regenerates that directory, a race between the resource glob and the Core bundle build. The application binary itself builds green (`--no-bundle`, exit 0).
remainingRisk: the NSIS installer cannot be produced until the core/bundle resource race is fixed (regenerate the bundle BEFORE tauri resolves the resources, or exclude the bundle from the installer resources). BLOCKED_EXTERNAL for the installer only.
